twice — **fully worked** (every step narrated, including the why), then a
**faded twin** where the middle steps are yours, each confirmed by a gate

## Part 1 — fully worked: the slider bearing

*A machine slide rides a 0.30 m × 0.30 m pad on a 0.4 mm film of SAE-30 oil
(μ = 0.29 Pa·s) at 1.5 m/s. Find the drag force and the power it burns.*

**Step 0 — the model.** Thin film, parallel walls, steady sliding: linear
Couette profile, so one slope and one stress everywhere in the film. (This
assumption — profile first, everything after — is the whole method.)

**Step 1 — stress.** $\tau = \mu U/h = 0.29 (1.5)/(4\times10^{-4})
= 1087$ Pa. *Why stress first:* it's the film's property, independent
of how big a pad rides on it.

**Step 2 — force.** $F = \tau A = 1087 \times 0.09 = 97.9$ N.
Geometry's turn: the area enters here and only here.

**Step 3 — power.** $P = F U = 97.9 \times 1.5 = 147$ W —
delivered continuously into the film as heat.[^heat]

[^heat]: Which warms the oil, which drops μ, which cuts the drag: bearings
partially self-medicate. It also caps how thin the designer dares run the
film — Unit 1's viscosity-temperature story with a maintenance budget.

## Part 2 — the faded twin: cold-start

*Same machine on a winter morning: the oil is at 0 °C where μ = 0.90 Pa·s.
A different slide: pad 0.20 m × 0.40 m, film 0.25 mm, speed 2.0 m/s.*

**Step 0 is on the house:** same linear-film model. You drive.

```{=html}
<div class="fl-checkpoint"
     data-prompt="Step 1 — shear stress in the cold film?"
     data-answer="7200" data-tol="0.03" data-units="Pa"
     data-hint="τ = μU/h with h = 0.25 mm = 2.5×10⁻⁴ m. Cold oil, thin film — this one is big."
     data-solution="τ = 0.90 × 2.0/2.5×10⁻⁴ = 7200 Pa."
     data-target="u1w-s2"></div>
```

::: {#u1w-s2 .fl-hidden}
✓ Twelve times Part 1's stress — cold μ and a thinner film, multiplied.

```{=html}
<div class="fl-checkpoint"
     data-prompt="Step 2 — drag force on the pad?"
     data-answer="576" data-tol="0.03" data-units="N"
     data-hint="F = τA, and the pad is 0.20 × 0.40 = 0.08 m²."
     data-solution="F = 7200 × 0.08 = 576 N — more than the weight of most of the machine."
     data-target="u1w-s3"></div>
```
:::

::: {#u1w-s3 .fl-hidden}
✓ This is why cold starts stall drives and snap couplings.

```{=html}
<div class="fl-checkpoint"
     data-prompt="Step 3 — power burned in the film at speed?"
     data-answer="1152" data-tol="0.03" data-units="W"
     data-hint="P = F·U. The motor pays this continuously until the film warms."
     data-solution="P = 576 × 2.0 = 1152 W into 20 grams of oil — it will not stay cold long."
     data-target="u1w-s4"></div>
```
:::

::: {#u1w-s4 .fl-hidden}
```{=html}
<div class="fl-checkpoint"
     data-prompt="Step 4 — at operating temperature μ falls to 0.06 Pa·s. New drag force?"
     data-answer="38.4" data-tol="0.03" data-units="N"
     data-hint="Everything scales linearly with μ here: multiply your Step-2 force by 0.06/0.90."
     data-solution="F = 576 × (0.06/0.90) = 38.4 N — a 15× discount, bought entirely by temperature."
     data-target="u1w-s5"></div>
```
:::

::: {#u1w-s5 .fl-hidden}
**What transferred.** Model → stress → force → power, with μ as the master
dial. The cold-start factor (here 15×) is a real design load case: motors,
couplings, and startup ramps are sized for the *winter* number.
:::

## Let the toolbox referee

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: false
for label, mu, h, A, U in [("Part 1 (SAE-30, warm)", 0.29, 4e-4, 0.09, 1.5),
                            ("Part 2 (cold start)",   0.90, 2.5e-4, 0.08, 2.0),
                            ("Part 2 (operating)",    0.06, 2.5e-4, 0.08, 2.0)]:
    tau = mu*U/h
    print(f"{label}: tau = {tau:,.0f} Pa   F = {tau*A:,.1f} N   P = {tau*A*U:,.0f} W")
```
